passage: Tuesday. Today Maya and her friends laughed at my new haircut in the corridor. I went and sat on the bench by the library and pretended to read. Then Rafiq came over and sat next to me. He did not say much. He just asked, "Are you okay?" and stayed there until the bell rang. That tiny thing made my throat go tight, but in a good way. I said thanks, and he shrugged like it was nothing. It was not nothing to me. I felt less alone than I have all week. Maybe one day I will sit next to somebody like that too. -- Jahnavi

qa.q: Where did Jahnavi sit after the laughing?
qa.a: Jahnavi sat on the bench by the library.

qa.q: Why did Jahnavi's throat go tight in a good way when Rafiq sat alongside?
qa.a: Jahnavi was touched by his kindness and felt less alone.

qa.q: How could Jahnavi pass this kindness on later?
qa.a: Jahnavi could sit beside someone who has been teased and quietly ask if they are okay.

qa.q: How might Rafiq see his own small act?
qa.a: He shrugged as though it was nothing, so he may not realise how much it meant to Jahnavi; he probably just wanted to make sure Jahnavi was okay.

grounding: A teased child records how one classmate's quiet company eased that loneliness.

passage:
"Akash, your Dhruv Dada was once the one being teased. At eleven I had big front teeth, and a group of boys called me 'rabbit' until I ran behind the school well and sat there with my head on my knees.
Then Vasant, a quiet boy from the back bench, came and sat next to me. He didn't say much. Just, 'Are you all right?' And he stayed until the bell.
It was such a small thing, but I still remember the warmth of it. We told our teacher together that afternoon, and she spoke to the boys.
Years later, I saw a small boy crying by the bus stand. I sat down next to him. That's how kindness travels."

qa.q: What did the boys call young Dhruv?
How did young Dhruv feel when Vasant sat next to him?
qa.a: He felt comforted and less alone; he still remembers the warmth of that small kindness.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story helped most after the teasing?
qa.a: Vasant sitting with him and asking if he was all right, then the two of them telling the teacher that afternoon.

qa.q: How might Vasant have felt going to sit with young Dhruv?
qa.a: Vasant, being quiet, may have felt shy but caring enough to act anyway.

grounding: A grandfather recalls a quiet classmate sitting with him after he was teased and asking if he was okay, a small kindness he later passed on.

passage:
Sports day was loud and crowded, and the rain kept threatening. After the relay, some girls called Hafsa "slowpoke" and laughed while she walked off the track.
Hafsa sat under the tin roof of the equipment shed, trying not to cry. Everyone was busy with the next race. Nobody noticed. Or so she thought.
Deepika ducked in, shaking water off her hair. She sat on an upturned bucket. "Are you okay? That was mean."
Hafsa shook her head. Deepika stayed, saying nothing, while the rain drummed.
When the rain stopped, they went together to tell Miss Joshi, who spoke to the girls before prize-giving. Hafsa thought: one day I'll do this for someone else.

qa.q: What did the girls call Hafsa?
What did Hafsa feel when Deepika sat with her?
qa.a: She felt less alone and grateful, even though she was still upset.

qa.q: What small kindness did Deepika show?
qa.a: She sat with Hafsa, asked if she was okay and stayed through the rain, then went with her to tell Miss Joshi.

qa.q: How might Deepika have seen the moment in the shed?
qa.a: Deepika may have felt it was simple but important to stay with someone who was hurt.

grounding: A girl teased after a race is found by a classmate who sits with her and asks if she is okay; the kindness means a lot and she plans to pass it on.
